title: Briarhold's browser release: keeping generated artwork consistent across dialogue and progression screens
author: Samfa12
selftext:
I've released the browser version of Briarhold alongside its Alpha.97 Android update. It's a free first-person fortress-defence game, and this update focused on illustrated conversations, progression presentation and navigation fixes.



I use AI extensively for coding assistance and visual asset creation. OpenAI image generation was used for the new portraits and icons; the wider project also uses Meshy-generated models prepared through Blender. This post was drafted with AI assistance too.



A useful lesson from this update was to establish the existing characters as references before generating their portraits. Five holdfolk portraits and 48 boon/upgrade emblems now share the same manuscript palette. The runtime images are compact WebP assets, with the icons packed into one atlas.



Existing 3D assets were reused, with material and lighting corrections taking priority over replacement geometry. No additional Meshy credits were needed for this update. Asset optimization also kept the Android APK about 1.45 MB smaller than the previous release despite the new interface art.



The difficult part was maintaining a consistent visual identity while preserving readable phone interfaces, existing save identifiers and purchase rules. Matching source/runtime views and testing the real progression states were more useful than judging a generated image in isolation.



Play in your browser: [https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/play/](https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/play/)

Android download and update: [https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/](https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/)



It's still an alpha, and co-op remains experimental. I'd be interested in how others keep generated character portraits consistent with existing in-game models across repeated updates.
